newsitem.title: USA: NASA sets date for shuttle Mir flight.
newsitem.headline: NASA sets date for shuttle Mir flight.

text.p: NASA officials on Wednesday cleared the space shuttle Atlantis for launch on a mission to pick up one U.S. astronaut and drop off another at the Russian Mir space station.
Atlantis would blast off on May 15 at 4:08 a.m. EDT (0804 GMT), senior space agency officials decided at a meeting held at the Kennedy Space Centre.

The shuttle was to dock two days later with the orbiting space station, where U.S. astronaut Jerry Linenger has worked since January. His place aboard Mir would be taken by British-born astronaut Michael Foale.
"Together with our Russian partners, we reviewed the status of Atlantis and the Mir station and have agreed that everything is ready," Johnson Space Centre director George Abbey said in statement.
A serious fire and problems with the station's life support systems had prompted NASA to closely scrutinise safety aboard the orbiting outpost before authorising Foale's four-month stay.
Visiting the Florida launch site earlier this week, Foale said he had no qualms about living aboard Mir. The recent difficulties had brought the two space-faring nations closer together, he said.
"I think we're learning the most when things don't quite go per the plan and we have to work together very hard to solve these problems," he said.
Foale will be the fifth U.S. astronaut to live on Mir. Two more are in training for future fights.
